# Rules

<!-- Generated by `node scripts/rules-doc.ts` from src/rules/catalog.ts. Do not edit by hand. -->

Each finding names one of these rules. Severity is the highest a rule reports; a
single finding can be rated lower, for example when plenger saw an input check or
an approval step. OWASP ids refer to the [Top 10 for LLM Applications
2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llm-top-10/) (`LLMxx:2025`) and the [Top 10 for Agentic
Applications 2026](https://genai.owasp.org/resource/owasp-top-10-for-agentic-applications-for-2026/)
(`ASIxx`).

## PLG101 tool-command-injection

**Tool runs a command the model controls.** Severity up to critical.

A tool builds a shell command, or names the program to run, from arguments the model chooses. Anyone who can influence the model, directly or through content it reads, can run commands with the agent's privileges.

**Fix:** Do not let the model write commands. Expose narrow tools that run a fixed program with an argument list and no shell, validate each argument against an allow-list, and run anything broader in a sandbox without credentials and behind human approval.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), ASI02, ASI05, [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-77](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/77.html)

## PLG102 tool-argument-injection

**Tool passes model input to a program's arguments.** Severity up to medium.

A tool runs a fixed program without a shell but passes arguments the model chooses. A value that starts with `-` can turn into an option (`--output=...`, `-c ...`) and change what the program does.

**Fix:** Validate arguments against an allow-list or a strict pattern, reject values that start with `-`, and put `--` before positional arguments where the program supports it.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI02, [CWE-88](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/88.html)

## PLG103 tool-code-execution

**Tool evaluates code the model controls.** Severity up to critical.

A tool evaluates model-chosen input as code (`eval`, `exec`, `Function`, `vm`, a Python REPL tool) in the agent's own process.

**Fix:** Replace evaluation with a parser for the narrow language the tool needs (an arithmetic parser, `ast.literal_eval`, JSON). If the tool must run code, run it in an isolated sandbox (container or remote) with no credentials or network.

**Maps to:** [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI05, [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-95](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/95.html)

## PLG104 tool-path-traversal

**Tool accesses a file path the model controls.** Severity up to high.

A tool reads, writes or deletes a file at a path built from model-chosen arguments. Without confinement the model can reach files outside the intended directory (`../../.env`, `/etc/passwd`).

**Fix:** Resolve the path (`os.path.realpath`, `path.resolve`), check that it stays inside an allowed base directory, refuse symlinks out of it, and prefer read-only access.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), [LLM02:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure/), ASI02, [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-73](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/73.html)

## PLG105 tool-ssrf

**Tool requests a URL the model controls.** Severity up to medium.

A tool fetches or opens a URL whose scheme or host the model chooses. The model can be steered to internal services and cloud metadata endpoints, or to send data to an outside server.

**Fix:** Allow only known hosts, resolve the host and reject private, loopback and link-local addresses, disable redirects to other hosts, and keep credentials out of requests the model shapes.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), [LLM02:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure/), ASI02, [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html)

## PLG106 tool-sql-injection

**Tool runs a database query the model controls.** Severity up to high.

A tool runs a SQL query written by the model or built from its arguments. The model can read or change any data the connection can reach.

**Fix:** Use parameterised queries with fixed SQL. If the model must write queries, use a read-only connection limited to the tables it needs, with a statement timeout, and review writes before they run.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), ASI02, [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html)

## PLG107 tool-unsafe-deserialization

**Tool deserializes data the model controls.** Severity up to high.

A tool loads model-chosen data, or data from a model-chosen location, with a deserializer that can run code (`pickle`, `yaml.unsafe_load`, `torch.load`).

**Fix:** Use a data-only format (JSON, `yaml.safe_load`, `safetensors`, `torch.load(weights_only=True)`) and never load files from locations the model chooses.

**Maps to:** [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), ASI05, [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

## PLG108 tool-outbound-action

**Tool sends messages or payments the model directs.** Severity up to high.

A tool sends a message to a recipient, or makes a payment of an amount, that the model chooses. Injected instructions can make the agent contact or pay anyone.

**Fix:** Restrict recipients and amounts to allow-lists or limits set by the application, not the model, and require human approval for each send or payment.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI02, ASI09

## PLG201 agent-unapproved-actions

**Agent can take high-impact actions with no human approval.** Severity up to high.

An agent can run commands, execute code, change files, databases or money, or send messages through its tools, and plenger saw no human approval step for those tools or the agent.

**Fix:** Require approval for high-impact tools (`needs_approval`, `interrupt_before`, `HumanInTheLoopMiddleware`, `needsApproval`), give the agent the fewest tools it needs, and log every action.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI02, ASI09

## PLG202 agent-local-code-execution

**Agent runs model-written code on the host.** Severity up to critical.

An agent executes the code the model writes in the application's own environment (a local executor, `code_execution_mode="unsafe"`, `use_docker=False`).

**Fix:** Run generated code in a container or remote sandbox (Docker, E2B, Modal) with no credentials, no access to the host file system and restricted network.

**Maps to:** [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI05, [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

## PLG203 agent-unbounded-loop

**Agent runs with no iteration limit.** Severity up to low.

An agent or multi-agent team has its turn, step or recursion limit removed, or has no termination condition, so a confused or manipulated model can loop without end and run up cost.

**Fix:** Set a turn or step limit (`max_turns`, `max_iterations`, `recursion_limit`, `stopWhen`) and a termination condition, plus a token or cost budget per request.

**Maps to:** [LLM10:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm102025-unbounded-consumption/), ASI08, [CWE-770](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/770.html), [CWE-834](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/834.html)

## PLG301 request-to-dangerous-agent

**HTTP input reaches an agent with high-impact tools.** Severity up to critical.

An HTTP route passes request input to an agent or model call that can run commands, execute code or change files, data or money. Prompt injection in the request turns into those actions.

**Fix:** Authenticate and rate-limit the route, separate untrusted input from instructions, remove high-impact tools from agents that serve untrusted users, and require human approval for the rest.

**Maps to:** [LLM01:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/), [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI01, ASI02, [CWE-1427](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1427.html)

## PLG302 system-prompt-injection

**Outside input is placed in the system prompt.** Severity up to high.

Text from a request or a function argument is placed into the system prompt (an f-string, or a template variable such as llmfy's `{{var}}` filled at the call). Instructions in that text get system-level authority.

**Fix:** Keep the system prompt fixed. Pass user and retrieved text in user messages, clearly delimited, and validate values that must go into the system prompt (an enum, a known name).

**Maps to:** [LLM01:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/), ASI01, [CWE-1427](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1427.html)

## PLG303 untrusted-content-in-system-prompt

**Retrieved or fetched content is placed in the system prompt.** Severity up to medium.

Documents from a retriever or vector store, or content fetched from the web, are placed into the system prompt. Anyone who can write those documents or pages can inject instructions (indirect prompt injection).

**Fix:** Pass retrieved content in a user or tool message, delimited and labelled as data, control who can write to the indexed sources, and limit what the agent can do after reading them.

**Maps to:** [LLM01:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm01-prompt-injection/), [LLM08:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm082025-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses/), ASI06, [CWE-1427](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1427.html)

## PLG401 model-output-to-sink

**Model output is used as a command, code, query, path or URL.** Severity up to critical.

The output of a model call or agent run flows into a command, code evaluation, query, file path, URL or deserializer without validation. Whoever steers the model controls that effect.

**Fix:** Treat model output as untrusted input: parse it into a strict schema, check values against allow-lists, and never pass it to a shell, `eval` or a query string.

**Maps to:** [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), ASI05, [CWE-1426](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1426.html), [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html), [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html), [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html)

## PLG501 hardcoded-model-key

**Model API key written in the code.** Severity up to high.

A model client is created with an API key written in the source. Anyone with access to the code, its history or a built artefact can use the key.

**Fix:** Revoke the key, load it from the environment or a secret manager, and remove it from version control history.

**Maps to:** ASI03, [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html)

## PLG502 secret-in-source

**Secret in source code.** Severity up to high.

A string in the source has the format of a known API key, token or private key.

**Fix:** Revoke the secret, load it from the environment or a secret manager, and remove it from version control history.

**Maps to:** ASI03, [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html)

## PLG503 secret-in-prompt

**Secret in a prompt.** Severity up to high.

A prompt contains an API key, token or password. Models repeat their prompts when asked the right way, so the secret can leak to users.

**Fix:** Remove the secret from the prompt and revoke it. Let tools use credentials on the server side; the model should never see them.

**Maps to:** [LLM07:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm072025-system-prompt-leakage/), [LLM02:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure/), ASI03, [CWE-200](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html), [CWE-798](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html)

## PLG601 mcp-server-no-auth

**MCP server exposes high-impact tools over HTTP with no authentication.** Severity up to high.

An MCP server served over HTTP (streamable HTTP or SSE) offers tools that run commands, execute code or change files or data, and plenger saw no authentication for it. Anyone who can reach the port can call them.

**Fix:** Require authentication (`auth=`, `token_verifier=`, `requireBearerAuth`), bind to localhost when only local clients need it, and authorise each tool call.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI02, ASI03, [CWE-306](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html)

## PLG602 mcp-unpinned-server

**MCP server started from an unpinned package.** Severity up to medium.

An MCP client starts a stdio server with `npx`, `uvx`, `pipx run` or `docker run` without a pinned version, so each start can run whatever the registry serves at that moment.

**Fix:** Pin an exact version (`pkg@1.2.3`, `pkg==1.2.3`, an image digest), or install the server as a locked dependency and start it from there.

**Maps to:** [LLM03:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/), ASI04, [CWE-829](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/829.html), [CWE-1357](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/1357.html)

## PLG603 mcp-plaintext-transport

**MCP client connects to a remote server over plain HTTP.** Severity up to low.

An MCP client connects to a non-local server with `http://`. Tool calls, results and any credentials travel unencrypted and can be read or changed on the way.

**Fix:** Use `https://` for every remote MCP server.

**Maps to:** ASI04, ASI07, [CWE-319](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/319.html)

## PLG701 dangerous-code-opt-in

**Framework allowed to run generated code.** Severity up to high.

A framework option that lets the model's code run is turned on (`allow_dangerous_code=True`, smolagents `additional_authorized_imports` with `*`, `os` or `subprocess`).

**Fix:** Turn the option off, or run the agent in an isolated sandbox with no credentials and only the imports it needs.

**Maps to:** [LLM05:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm052025-improper-output-handling/), ASI05, [CWE-94](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/94.html)

## PLG702 unsafe-deserialization-opt-in

**Framework allowed to load pickled data.** Severity up to high.

`allow_dangerous_deserialization=True` lets a vector store or loader unpickle files. Anyone who can replace those files can run code when they are loaded.

**Fix:** Load only files the application created and stores where others cannot write, or rebuild the index from source documents instead of loading pickles.

**Maps to:** [LLM03:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/), [LLM08:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm082025-vector-and-embedding-weaknesses/), ASI04, [CWE-502](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/502.html)

## PLG703 remote-code-trust

**Model loading trusts code from the model repository.** Severity up to high.

`trust_remote_code=True` runs Python code shipped with a model or dataset from the hub when it is loaded.

**Fix:** Prefer models that do not need remote code; otherwise pin the exact revision (`revision=` a commit hash) after reviewing its code.

**Maps to:** [LLM03:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm032025-supply-chain/), ASI04, [CWE-494](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/494.html)

## PLG704 api-key-in-browser

**Model SDK allowed in the browser.** Severity up to high.

`dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true` runs the model SDK in the browser, so the API key is shipped to every visitor.

**Fix:** Call the model from a server route that holds the key, or use short-lived, scoped tokens issued per user.

**Maps to:** [LLM02:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm022025-sensitive-information-disclosure/), ASI03, [CWE-522](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/522.html)

## PLG705 dangerous-requests-opt-in

**Framework allowed to make arbitrary HTTP requests.** Severity up to medium.

`allow_dangerous_requests=True` lets an agent's request tools call any URL the model chooses, including internal services.

**Fix:** Give the agent tools for specific APIs instead, or put an allow-list of hosts in front of the request tools.

**Maps to:** [LLM06:2025](https://genai.owasp.org/llmrisk/llm062025-excessive-agency/), ASI02, [CWE-918](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html)

## PLG801 route-command-injection

**Route runs a command built from request input.** Severity up to critical.

An HTTP route handler, or a project function it calls, builds a shell command, names the program to run or passes program arguments from the request. Anyone who can send the request can run commands with the application's privileges.

**Fix:** Run a fixed program with an argument list and no shell, check each request value against an allow-list or a strict pattern, and put `--` before positional arguments.

**Maps to:** [CWE-78](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/78.html), [CWE-77](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/77.html), [CWE-88](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/88.html)

## PLG802 route-path-traversal

**Route accesses a file path built from request input.** Severity up to high.

An HTTP route handler, or a project function it calls, reads, writes or deletes a file at a path built from the request. Without confinement a request can reach files outside the intended directory (`../../.env`).

**Fix:** Resolve the path (`os.path.realpath`, `Path.resolve`, `path.resolve`), check that it stays inside the base directory (`is_relative_to`, or a prefix that ends with a separator), or accept only names that match a strict pattern.

**Maps to:** [CWE-22](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/22.html), [CWE-73](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/73.html)

## PLG803 route-sql-injection

**Route runs a SQL query built from request input.** Severity up to high.

An HTTP route handler, or a project function it calls, puts request values into the text of a SQL query. A request can read or change any data the connection can reach.

**Fix:** Use parameterised queries: fixed SQL with placeholders (`?`, `%s`, `$1`, `:name`) and the request values passed separately.

**Maps to:** [CWE-89](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html)
